correctness.rationale: With the specified target norm, the images of the Hardy monomials are orthogonal and have lengths (k+1)^(-alpha)|sum_j a_j rho_j^k|, tending to zero. At L=t^(-1/alpha), count those with (k+1)/L below the 1/alpha power of the modulus. On a bounded window containing all such indices, character tests against continuous functions of (k+1)/L converge to the Lebesgue-Haar product: geometric partial sums are bounded for every nontrivial character and summation by parts handles the slow factor. The threshold graph has product measure zero by its singleton x-sections, even when the orbit distribution has atoms or exact cancellations. Integrating the subgraph gives M_alpha; the squared modulus has Haar mean sum_j |a_j|^2 by distinctness, so M_alpha>0. Inversion of the strict count yields s_n~M_alpha^alpha n^(-alpha) and harmonic summation gives the critical residue. For the equal two-term example the finite cosine sum is 1+2 sum_{k=1}^{floor((b-1)/2)} cos(pi k/b); the Dirichlet kernel formula yields the two parity values, including b=1 (coincident rotations combined) and b=2 (zeros on odd indices). On irrational orbits the mean is 4/pi. Rational denominators tending to infinity give that same limit, with strict finite-denominator inequalities in opposite directions. The diagonal difference bound k|theta-phi|/(k+1) independently gives norm Lipschitz continuity. No numerical premise is needed.

value.rationale: An exact tail constant for a natural class of compact superpositions quantifies cancellations that individual ideal memberships do not detect. The two-term example gives sharp rational values and demonstrates a genuine instability of the critical residue in an operator-norm Lipschitz family, not an instability of operator norm itself. The elementary ingredients do not make the combined spectral and arithmetic conclusion vacuous.
